channel.title: Hesed Words — Reflections
channel.description: Devotional reflections by Norm Reed. Scripture, justice, and the love that holds. Written for the road.

item.title: Notes for the Band
item.description: The psalm sat flat, so I went looking for a hook and found one above it. A lifetime of reading the heading as small print meant for somebody else.

item.title: What They Sang
item.description: Judah's singers walked out ahead of the army with one line. It asks for nothing, and says nothing about the outcome.

item.title: The Cause I Applied For
item.description: A grant knocked back, and two years before the reason arrived. Psalm 74 was written by a man who never finds out.

item.title: Succession Planning — Everything Set in Place
item.description: David prepared everything for Solomon. The temple was built exactly as it was drawn. The kingdom lasted one generation.

item.title: Love Your Enemies — What Psalm 68 Will Not Let You Do
item.description: A commandant in a wartime detention camp handed back the sermon script and cancelled the service: you don't love us, your enemies. Psalm 68 gives permission to have enemies and no permission at all to deal with them.

item.title: Telling David's Census to an Eight-Year-Old
item.description: A king counts his people and seventy thousand die. The verse the chapter ends on reads like a footnote, and is the hinge of the whole thing.

item.title: Parables — You'll See
item.description: A phrase arrived six months before I could explain it — Lewis's ‘weight of glory’. Then a Sunday sermon on the treasure and the pearl, and a morning that came apart.

item.title: Kept Anyway
item.description: A reflection on 1 Chronicles 4:9–10 — Jabez, the nine chapters of genealogy nobody reads, and what it means to be remembered before anyone writes it down.

item.title: God Alone
item.description: Psalm 62 leans six times on ak, a fencing word — only, alone, nothing more. David commands his own soul to be still, is battered, and has to command it again. Written from the far side of a cardiac arrest.

item.title: The Piece I Keep Picking Up
item.description: Reading to the end of Zechariah and not finishing it. The book had every reason to end on the throne, or at the open door in the mountain. It ends in a kitchen, with someone reaching for a pot.

item.title: The One Thing He Wouldn't Delegate
item.description: A young man in Zechariah's second vision is stopped mid-survey — the cord was not the wrong instrument, just not the last word. A hard man in Papua New Guinea handed over every authority except the one to be merciful.

item.title: The Vow?
item.description: Psalm 61 asks four times for a place, and every shelter in it has an owner. Then a vow appears and the prayer tilts: heard first, performed last, with the shelter sitting in between. Not the shape of a bargain.

item.title: What Is Wicked in This Story?
item.description: Psalm 58 ends with the righteous bathing their feet in the blood of the wicked — unusable, until verse one turns out to say who it's actually addressed to. Not criminals. The bench.

item.title: Those Who Know Their God
item.description: Daniel 11:32 promises the people who know their God shall be strong and do exploits — a verse that once became, for a young Christian with an explanation for every date, a chapter about knowing better instead of knowing God.

item.title: This I Know
item.description: Psalm 56 never says we, only I. Batach — to lean your whole weight on something and find out whether it holds. This I know, that God is for me — a line that only comes after the tossings have been numbered.

item.title: Pride
item.description: Waking with thoughts upon the bed, like Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 4 — and the discovery that pride never feels like pride from the inside, only ever like accuracy. The verdict we reach about our own humility is useless.
